disposition_reason: Table 4 prints one dry-weight concentration per element for each of seven Tabbouli ingredients grown in Lebanese allotments.

study.design: field survey of soils and edible plant parts used in Tabbouli salad, three communal allotments
study.origin: Damour (parsley, lemon), Ghazir (olive, onion), Akkar (peppermint, tomato), Lebanon; bulgur source not stated
study.method: ICP-OES after microwave digestion HNO3/H2O2 (6:1) for plants; aqua regia and 0.43 M acetic acid for soils
study.qa: triplicate analysis, blanks; plant CRM recovery ~100% (unnamed); soil CRMs NIST SRM 2709, 2711a, BCR-483, BCR-484

unresolved: Soil results (Tables 2, 3) and transfer factors (Table 6) are not findings.
Table 4 descriptive statistics (mean, median, SD across the seven different plants) are cross-food summaries and not recorded as findings.
Table 5 per-portion amounts (mg per ingredient in a 100 g Tabbouli plate) are derived, not measured; the text gives tomato as 280 g in methods and 240 g on p. 160.
Table 6 lists a 'Cucumber' row identical to parsley although cucumber was not sampled.
The number of plant samples per species is not stated.
